description: Descriptive Copilot Chat model metadata for APEX. Active production agent definitions omit model and reasoning-effort pins; the operator and runtime control selection, including Auto and HydraFusion. Worker readiness is model-agnostic. `assignments` is generated from any explicit legacy fixture pins and is empty for active agents. Static catalog checks do not certify worker readiness or runtime tool binding.

GPT-6.1 Sol (copilot).notes: Requested exact label; availability and runtime effort controls require manual verification. Utility prompts use it; the five step agents moved to Claude Sonnet 5.5 and the label stays authorized. Agents on this label use reasoning-effort: high.

GPT-6 Sol (copilot).notes: Requested exact label; availability and runtime effort controls require manual verification. No active assignment since the 2026-09 Claude migration; stays authorized.

GPT-6 Luna (copilot).notes: Requested exact label; availability and runtime effort controls require manual verification.

Claude Opus 5.5 (copilot).notes: Requested exact label; availability and runtime effort controls require manual verification. No active assignment after the step agents moved to Claude Sonnet 5.5; stays authorized.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (copilot).notes: Requested exact label; availability and runtime effort controls require manual verification. Requirements, Architect, IaC Planner, Challenger and Context Optimizer use reasoning-effort: high; all other agents use reasoning-effort: medium.

GPT-5.6 Terra (copilot).notes: Balanced GPT-5.6 tier for Local utility prompts. Prompting follows OpenAI's GPT-5.6 prompt guidance plus the APEX outcome-first convention.

MAI-Code-1.1-Flash.notes: Microsoft's fast, cost-optimized coding model. Authorized 2026-06 for the Orchestrator (01), which performs handoff-only routing with no creative generation — a lightweight standard-tier model is sufficient. No MAI-specific automated prompting rules exist yet; the `mai-code` family is `reviewer-only` in vendor-prompting (see `.github/skills/apex-vendor-prompting/references/family-support.md`). The orchestrator body retains its outcome-first skeleton (Role/Goal/Success/Constraints/Output/Stop), which remains a sound structure for a routing agent.

governance.source_of_truth: The operator and runtime control model selection; active definitions do not assign it. Model names, effort, picker selection and model-source labels are diagnostic only, not readiness gates. Optional registry and catalog assignments preserve explicit legacy fixture pins. The catalog models block preserves descriptive metadata; generated assignments must match explicit pins (enforced by validate-models.mjs --only=catalog).
rules: Any explicit legacy model pin in agent or subagent frontmatter MUST exist as a key in `models`.
Any explicit legacy model value in the agent registry MUST exist as a key in `models` and match its corresponding frontmatter pin.
The `assignments` block MUST match the output of `node tools/scripts/generate-model-catalog.mjs`; active production definitions are unpinned, so their generated maps are empty.
A model with `deprecated: true` MAY remain in `models` for audit history but MUST NOT appear in any explicit active legacy pin.

assignments.description: Auto-generated inventory of explicit legacy agent → model pins. Active production definitions are unpinned, so their maps are intentionally empty. Do not edit by hand; run `node tools/scripts/generate-model-catalog.mjs`.
